input.prompt:
Hill-climb opening move (task #13) in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, single H100. CONTEXT: the L3-TC persistent megakernel (fwd+bwd+opt fused, wgmma) was just proven END-TO-END at d=1024 on the decoder (parity 2.4e-07, A/A/A) — but at 0.49% of the compute roofline at BOTH d=128 and d=1024 (d=1024: 4.865 TF/s achieved, 0.5 steps/s @ B=16384, i.e. 2 SECONDS per step for ~10 PFLOP that 30% MFU would do in ~33 ms). The naive "% climbs with d" premise is refuted; the inefficiency is in the kernel/engine structure. Before ANY optimization, we need (A) loop infrastructure and (B) an evidence-grade diagnosis of where the 2 s/step goes.

HEAD=555c0bc (includes the SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL decouple gate, so the decoder TC TU builds at large d). The d=1024 procedure is PROVEN: set SG_DEC_D=1024 in csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh via megakernel_codegen.py regen + decoder oracle lockstep (the prior builder did exactly this — find its method in git log / the layout codegen; static_asserts enforce correctness). Production = d=128; 33/33 cells green via `python wiring_check.py --require-all`.

DELIVERABLE A — PERSISTENT BENCHMARK-VARIANT BUILD (the hill-climb loop infra):
Make the d-scaled decoder benchmark a FIRST-CLASS coexisting build, so each hill-climb iteration does NOT redo throwaway codegen/revert. Find the cleanest mechanism, e.g.: a second extension module (_ops_bench) built from the same sources with SG_DEC_D=1024 + a distinct module/extension name + its own build dir, importable alongside the production _ops; or an env-keyed parallel layout header. Constraints: production _ops.so and the 33/33 gate stay untouched; the variant rebuilds incrementally (sccache, build_ext --inplace pattern); tree stays committable (commit the infra once production stays green — run wiring_check --require-all to prove it). Document the exact rebuild+measure command for one hill-climb iteration (edit shared header -> rebuild variant -> measure) in a new file /workspace/.hillclimb_loop.md.

DELIVERABLE B — PHASE-LEVEL TIME BREAKDOWN of one d=1024 adamw/decoder step (the diagnosis):
Where do the 2 seconds go? Produce a per-phase wall breakdown: P1 fwd+bwd (the wgmma GEMM work), grid barriers (count x cost), P2 dW assembly (+split-K), P2.x/P3 optimizer tail, plus host/launch overhead. Methods in order of preference: (1) in-kernel phase timers if the kernel already has any (grep for clock64/timing scaffolding); (2) nsys profile of a few steps (nsys profile -t cuda --stats=true python ...) — note the megakernel is ONE launch so nsys gives kernel-total only, which is still useful to split host-vs-device; (3) ncu section metrics for the launch (sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active, dram throughput, achieved occupancy, warp stall reasons — `ncu --set full` on one step, the most informative for WHERE cycles stall); (4) cheapest decisive instrument: temporary clock64() phase-stamp writes to a debug buffer at each GridBarrier boundary (P0/B0/P1/B1/P2/B2/P3 + final), one CTA's worth, printed host-side — this gives the EXACT per-phase split with ~zero perturbation. You may instrument TEMPORARILY; keep the instrumentation OUT of the committed production path (variant-only or revert it; a committed opt-in debug flag default-OFF is acceptable if clean).
Use B=16384 (the measured config) + also one smaller B (e.g. 2048) to see if the split shifts. 3 repeats, report medians.

REPORT (raw numbers): the per-phase ms + % table at d=1024 (and the small-B comparison), warp-stall/tensor-pipe-utilization highlights if ncu was used, your top-3 hypotheses for the 0.49% RANKED BY EVIDENCE (e.g. serial K-loop in the per-CTA GEMM, barrier serialization, dW dominating, smem pipeline stalls, occupancy=1 ceiling, launch/host gaps), and the single highest-leverage first optimization candidate for the hill-climb. NO optimization edits yet — diagnosis only. Final state: production green (wiring 33/33), variant build committed if green, instrumentation not in the production path.

| P1_fwd | 22.1% (525 ms) | 18.4% | 8.7% |
| P1_bwd | **24.0% (572 ms)** | 20.3% | 8.8% |
| B1 barrier | 12.4% (296 ms) | **41.3% (260 ms)** | 6.6% |

1. **Per-CTA GEMM runs at <1% tensor-core MFU — serialized wgmma (occupancy=1 ceiling).** Strongest evidence: at d=1024 the GEMM phases (P1_fwd+P1_bwd+P2_dW = **64.3%**) are the bulk, yet total MFU is 0.48%; and P2_dW has 12,352 split-K work items over 132 SMs (94 waves — *not* SM-starved), so its inefficiency is intrinsic per-CTA, not tiling. The ptxas **C7515** warning fires on every build: *"wgmma.mma_async serialized due to non-wgmma instructions defining accumulator registers between start/end of the pipeline stage"* — the wgmma pipeline never overlaps. Persistent megakernel = 1 CTA/SM (occupancy=1), so there's no second warp-group to hide wgmma latency. This is the **highest-leverage** lever.
2. **P2 grad-assembly is an O(V·d·T) brute-force embedding scan that should be O(d·T).** `dectc_embed_owner_scan` (csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1295) has each of ~99 owner-CTAs *linearly scan all T tokens with a branch* (`if tok_ids[t]==r`) and uncoalesced strided `dh0` reads — re-reading the entire activation V times. It **dominates at d=128 (65.6%)** and is still **21.9% at d=1024** (should be ~0). A scatter-add / sort-segment-reduce kills the V× redundancy and the load imbalance (only 99/132 CTAs work; threads>d idle).
3. **Grid-barrier serialization from P1 load imbalance.** Barriers are 13.4% at B=16384 but **41.6% at B=2048**, where n_tiles=64 < nCTA=132 → ~half the SMs do zero P1 tiles and spin at B1. The 6-barrier-per-step rendezvous (B0/B1/B2 + opt sub-barriers) serializes on the slowest CTA; exposed badly at small B, structural at all B.

## Single highest-leverage first optimization candidate

**Fix the per-CTA wgmma GEMM pipeline so the tensor core actually overlaps (hypothesis 1).** It owns 64% of d=1024 wall and the whole kernel is pinned at occupancy=1, so the C7515 serialization is paid with no latency hiding — the largest single bucket and the root of the "0.49% at every d." Concretely: restructure the wgmma accumulator lifetime so no non-wgmma instruction writes the accumulator regs mid-pipeline (clear C7515), and/or add a producer/consumer warp-specialized smem pipeline (`tile_pipeline.cuh` is already included) so the single resident CTA hides wgmma/TMA latency. The embed-scan rewrite (hypothesis 2) is a cheaper, lower-risk *parallel* win (recovers ~22% at d=1024, ~66% at d=128) and is the obvious second move; barrier/load-balance (hypothesis 3) is third. No optimization edits were made — diagnosis only.</result>

input.description: H1: unserialize the wgmma pipeline
input.prompt:
Hill-climb move H1 (task #13) in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, single H100 — THE highest-leverage optimization: un-serialize the per-CTA wgmma GEMM pipeline in the L3-TC decoder megakernel. HEAD=79d3840.

EVIDENCE (from the committed clock64 phase profiler, SG_DEC_PROFILE): at d=1024 B=16384 the step is 2090.9 ms = 0.48% MFU; GEMM phases own 64% of wall (P1_fwd 22.1% + P1_bwd 24.0% + P2_dW 18.2%). ptxas emits C7515 on EVERY build: "wgmma.mma_async serialized due to non-wgmma instructions defining accumulator registers between start/end of the pipeline stage" — the wgmma pipeline never overlaps. The kernel is persistent one-CTA-per-SM (occupancy=1), so there is NO second resident warp-group to hide latency: the serialization is paid raw. Decoder TC regs are only 128-166 (headroom exists). The GEMM microkernel lives in csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh (dectc_gemm_fwd/_f32/_dx_f32 ~:378-435, dW tiles ~:1209-1270); tile_pipeline.cuh is already included. kTileM=128, TILE_N=128, 2-stage smem staging.

GOAL: clear the C7515 serialization and overlap the wgmma pipeline so the tensor pipe stays busy. Candidate techniques, in rough order of risk:
(a) Accumulator-lifetime restructure: ensure no non-wgmma instruction writes the wgmma accumulator registers between wgmma.fence/commit boundaries — restructure the K-loop so accumulator init (zeroing/scale) happens outside the pipelined region, epilogue reads happen only after the final commit+wait, and per-stage smem pointer arithmetic doesn't touch accumulator regs. Verify C7515 disappears from the ptxas output (the build log).
(b) Deepen the smem pipeline (2 -> 3-4 stages) with proper wgmma.commit_group/wait_group<N> overlap so TMA loads of stage k+1 overlap wgmma of stage k.
(c) Warp-specialized producer/consumer split within the CTA (producer warps drive TMA, consumer warp-groups issue wgmma) — the biggest restructure; only if (a)+(b) stall.
Iterate with the committed loop: edit -> `python tuning/decoder_bench.py --d 1024 --B 16384 --reps 3` (incremental, ~minutes) -> compare TF/s + steps/s vs the 2090.9 ms / 4.739 TF/s baseline -> keep if better, revert if not. Use `--profile` to see the per-phase shift. Also re-measure at d=128 B=16384 occasionally (production scale must not regress).

HARD GATES for any KEPT change (the campaign's discipline — never weaken):
- Parity: d=1024 bench vs the decoder oracle (the same gate the prior builder used) within tol + A/A/A bit-identical across 3 runs. The GEMM restructure MUST stay deterministic: fixed reduction order, no atomics, same accumulation order per output tile (a changed K-loop iteration ORDER changes the float sum — keep the ascending-k order so parity holds bitwise where it held before; if a pipeline depth change reorders accumulation, parity tolerance applies but A/A/A bitwise-identity across reruns is NON-NEGOTIABLE).
- Production: `python wiring_check.py --require-all` = 33/33 AND tail-gate `python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell adamw/decoder` + `--cell muon/decoder` green at d=128 after rebuilding production _ops (the edited header is shared by all decoder cells).
- These are PORTABLE components: keep the fix in the shared GEMM helpers (it should lift vit/mamba twins when propagated later); no per-cell hacks.
COMMIT when green with the measured numbers in the message. If a technique fails parity/determinism irreconcilably, revert it and try the next; report honestly.

DELIVERABLE: the kept change(s) + commit hash; BEFORE/AFTER raw numbers (ms/step, TF/s, MFU% at d=1024 B=16384; the per-phase table; C7515 present/absent in the final build log); d=128 production check results; what you tried that did NOT work and why. No report files — final message only.

input.prompt:
CPU-lane authoring task (Phase-2 pre-work per /workspace/.parallelism_design.md) in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. STRICT CONSTRAINTS: a kernel builder owns the GPU + the existing kernel files right now. You may ONLY create NEW files; do NOT edit ANY existing repo file (no megakernel headers, no dispatch.py/cpp, no setup.py); do NOT rebuild the _ops extension; do NOT run GPU kernels. Compile-checks via `nvcc -c` to a scratch dir (/dev/shm/tmp) only. Commit the new files when they compile-check clean (new files can't break production).

Read /workspace/.parallelism_design.md fully first (the contract), then author the 1-GPU-pre-testable pieces it specifies in §1, §2.3, §7 — as NEW standalone files:

1. csrc/fused/sm_90/parallel_config.cuh — the ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,SP,ZeROStage> template exactly per design §1.1 (constexpr fields, kIsSingleGPU/kEmitComm/kShardParams/kShardOptGrad/kTPComm/kPPStage, SP static_assert==1, using SingleGPU = ...). Header-only, self-contained, compilable standalone (nvcc -c a tiny .cu that includes it and static_asserts the SingleGPU properties).

2. csrc/fused/sm_90/sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh — per design §2.3: template <OptId Opt, class Par> sharded_optimizer_kernel(params_shard, grad_shard, lr, step, FusedOptState st_shard) as a flat grid-stride over [0, shard_numel) calling the EXISTING apply_optimizer<Opt> from opt_components.cuh (INCLUDE it, do not edit it; reuse the canonical math — zero new math). Note in comments the per-TENSOR cells (muon/SG11/15/SG2) need the tensor-granular shard + their P2.x stages (out of scope for this kernel; document the boundary per design §2.3/§3.4). Compile-check instantiations for the elementwise OptIds (adamw, lion, grokfast, grokadamw-elementwise-core, prodigy-elementwise-core...) — whatever apply_optimizer supports cleanly standalone; report which OptIds compile-check and which need kernel-stage context.

3. tests/hw/test_parallel_instantiation.py — per design §7.2: a CPU-only test that nvcc -c compiles the allow-list of ParConfig points (<SingleGPU>, <8,1,1,1,Z2>, <8,1,1,1,Z3>, <4,1,2,1,Z3>, <2,4,1,1,Z3>) against a minimal harness .cu; marked so it SKIPS when nvcc is absent. 4. grokking_optimizers/parallel/__init__.py + grokking_optimizers/parallel/shard_map.py — the tensor-granular partition per design §3.4: partition_tensor_granular(named_sizes, world) (greedy by numel, whole tensors, balanced) + the elementwise even-partition helper; pure Python + a pure-Python unit test tests/test_shard_map.py (no torch.distributed needed — pure functions on size lists; run it green with pytest).

Style: match the repo's header/comment conventions (read 2-3 existing headers first). Every file cites the design doc section it implements. Run the two runnable tests (3: nvcc compile test, 4: pytest shard-map test) and include their output. Commit ONLY the new files (git add <each new path>; commit message "phase-2 pre-work: parallelism config + sharded-opt kernel + shard map (design §1/§2.3/§3.4/§7.2, 1-GPU-authorable)"). Confirm `git status` shows no modification to any pre-existing file. Final message: files created, test outputs (raw), which OptIds compile-check in the sharded kernel, commit hash.

content.description: Analysis found nvcc TUs are uncached (sccache absent) → every build recompiles the whole extension. Install sccache so compile.py's PYTORCH_NVCC='sccache nvcc' path engages and only changed TUs recompile. Prerequisite for a fast overnight loop.

content.subject: Fix prodigy x3 NaN
content.description: DONE: decoder+vit prodigy NaN FIXED + committed (73e7170). Root cause = TWO defects: (1) ragged-tile GEMM OOB read clobbering Prodigy reduce slots -> NaN on reused buffers (m_atoms clamp, peer); (2) work-steal reduction non-determinism -> fixed-partition flat reduce (this agent). def test_export_merge_roundtrip():
    import json
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    jp = os.path.join(d, "_kernel_tuned.json")

    ok1 = ti.export_winner(
        "adamw", "decoder", "sm_90a",
        {"block": 128, "vec": 2, "unroll": 4, "async_depth": 3,
         "maxrregcount": 64, "timing_ms": 1.23, "config_key": "deadbeef",
         "cluster_shape": (2, 1, 1)},  # tuple dim must NOT be persisted.
        path=jp)
    check(ok1, "export_winner adamw returned True")
    ok2 = ti.export_winner(
        "muon", "vit", "sm_90",
        {"block": 256, "vec": 4, "unroll": 1, "async_depth": 2,
         "maxrregcount": 0},
        path=jp)
    check(ok2, "export_winner muon returned True")

    data = json.load(open(jp, encoding="utf-8"))
    # both winners survive the merge under the short "sm_90" key.
    check("sm_90" in data, "sm_90 arch key present")
    check("adamw" in data["sm_90"] and "muon" in data["sm_90"],
          "both adamw and muon winners present after merge")
    # only the safe per-TU dims (+ model provenance) persisted; internal
    # autotuner keys and tuple dims dropped.
    a = data["sm_90"]["adamw"]
    eq(a["block"], 128, "adamw block persisted")
    eq(a["maxrregcount"], 64, "adamw maxrregcount persisted")
    eq(a.get("model"), "decoder", "adamw model provenance persisted")
    check("timing_ms" not in a, "timing_ms NOT persisted")
    check("config_key" not in a, "config_key NOT persisted")
    check("cluster_shape" not in a, "cluster_shape (tuple) NOT persisted")
    # _meta present.
    check("_meta" in data and "timestamp" in data["_meta"],
          "_meta with timestamp present")

    # load_tuned reads it back identically.
    rt = ti.load_tuned(jp)
    eq(rt["sm_90"]["muon"]["vec"], 4, "load_tuned round-trips muon vec")

    # export_winner must NEVER raise / must return False on a bad path,
    # never propagate (fail-closed). Use a path whose "directory" is actually
    # an existing FILE, so os.makedirs() raises NotADirectoryError — a case
    # the exporter must catch and return False for (a failed persist can never

<result>Everything is committed and verified. All deliverables are complete. Let me provide the final report.

## Summary

**KEPT CHANGE — M-atom-interleaved wgmma GEMM pipeline** in the shared `dectc` GEMM helper. Commit **`627d134`** (`627d1340e143292e931909aaf54fbab2c3193a7b`) on branch `claude/h100-audit-maximal` (HEAD was 79d3840, now a4ba49f via other landed work; 79d3840 is an ancestor).

**What it does** (`csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`, + smem sizing in `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` `DecTcSmem`, + selftest arena in `decoder_tc_selftest.cu`): the K-chain used to run each stacked m64 atom to completion serially, re-staging the shared B (weight) tile **once per atom** and waiting after every wgmma. Now atoms run in groups of `kIL = min(MaxAtomsM, 2)`; within a group each K-step issues the 2 atom-wgmmas back-to-back into **independent fp32 fragments sharing one staged B-tile**. This (1) lets the tensor pipe overlap the two independent MMAs, and (2) **halves the HBM weight-operand traffic** (the actual bottleneck). Capped at 2 so accumulator-reg/A-smem stay bounded (dW tiles can be 8 atoms → 4 groups of 2; dW production is 1 atom → unchanged). Ascending-k accumulation per output element is untouched → bitwise-identical.

**BEFORE / AFTER (single H100, committed decoder_bench):**
- **d=1024 B=16384: 2084.25 → 1624.74 ms/step (−22.1%); 4.754 → 6.099 TF/s (+28.3%); MFU 0.48% → 0.62%**
- Per-phase (clock64): **P1_fwd 525.6→301.9 ms (−42.6%), P1_bwd 571.7→328.6 ms (−42.5%)** — exactly the 2-atom fwd/dX GEMMs; P2_dW 433→438 ms unchanged (kIL=1 by design, confirming the mechanism). New dominant phase is P2_grad_asm (not a GEMM).
- **d=128 B=16384 (production): 107.63 → 105.82 ms/step (−1.7%, no regression)** — clean back-to-back IL=1 vs IL=2 measurement (the first "regression" reading was concurrent-build contamination).

**HARD GATES (all green):**
- d=1024 A/A/A: params + state + loss (4.595632) bit-identical ×3.
- `wiring_check --require-all`: **33/33** cells on L3-TC.
- tail-gate `adamw/decoder` + `muon/decoder` (d=128, after `_ops` rebuild): **PASS** — state vs eager m≤2.2e-7/v≤9.6e-7 (adamw), 0/0 (muon); A/A/A bit-identical.
- `test_decoder_tc.py`: **18/18** (fwd/dX/dW across shapes incl. Nout=512→8-atom/4-group, dW determinism, full-cell oracle parity).

**C7515 status: STILL PRESENT** (1×; 255 regs / **0 spills** / 17844B smem at d=1024; stack dropped 1152→640B). The win is the within-group MMA overlap + B-staging-sharing, **not** C7515 removal — the cross-k single-fragment accumulator chain is inherently dependency-serialized, and true cross-k multi-in-flight needs the cp.async producer/consumer ring (large rewrite, deferred).

**What did NOT work (reverted):**
- **Single-fragment accumulator-lifetime restructure** (technique a, peel k=0 + one live fragment): pushed the kernel to 255 regs **+ 5180B spill stores / 5204B spill loads** (worse than baseline's 0 spills), and **did not clear C7515**. content.subject: Install sccache for fast CUDA-TU caching
content.description: Analysis found nvcc TUs are uncached (sccache absent) → every build recompiles the whole extension. Install sccache so compile.py's PYTORCH_NVCC='sccache nvcc' path engages and only changed TUs recompile. Prerequisite for a fast overnight loop.

content.subject: Fix prodigy x3 NaN
content.description: DONE: decoder+vit prodigy NaN FIXED + committed (73e7170). Root cause = TWO defects: (1) ragged-tile GEMM OOB read clobbering Prodigy reduce slots -> NaN on reused buffers (m_atoms clamp, peer); (2) work-steal reduction non-determinism -> fixed-partition flat reduce (this agent). Both required. Gates: A/A/A deterministic, tail-gate 19/19, initcheck 0. prodigy.h unchanged (no manifest/ABI). mamba/prodigy land-dormant (dispatch-gated; shared determinism concern). Build fast-path = setup.py build_ext --inplace.

content.subject: Commit verified in-flight cells

content.subject: Convert SG2 x3 to L3-TC
content.description: DONE: SG2 -> L3-TC on decoder+vit (commit 66b0f97, 30/33). Segmented sort (strategy A, stable-sort lock-step with oracle — ~413 real |grad| ties confirmed), meta-net composed (reused sg2_meta_stages + SAM 2nd-pass), dedicated ops.sg2_fused_step (per-tensor scalars don't fit FusedScalars). content.subject: Stage 1: ship tuned winners + add tile/split-K dims

content.activeForm: Authoring autotuner timer fix + tile dims (#12 prep)

content.subject: Stage 3: roofline hill-climb at d=2048 (owner-authorized)
content.description: Owner authorized + clarified: an OPTIMIZATION LOOP UNTIL CONVERGENCE, not one-shot. Per cell: propose optimization (multi-CTA tiling / tile size / split-K / pipe-depth / smem / occupancy / autotuner winner) -> incremental rebuild (sccache) -> measure roofline % via tuning/roofline.py (min-of-N, quiet GPU) -> KEEP if % improves beyond the measurement-noise floor AND parity stays green, else REVERT -> repeat until K consecutive attempts yield no improvement = that cell converged (its ceiling). Then next cell. Final cross-cell sweep: components are shared, so a component-level win can lift multiple cells -> re-measure all. Run at d=2048 (adjustable 1024/4096 - flag before heavy GPU). Prereqs: all 33 cells built out + multi-CTA tiling infra (#14).

content.subject: Stage-3 prep: multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling infrastructure
content.description: Overflow/Stage-3-prep, scale-INDEPENDENT: lift the one-CTA-per-SM cap (the real roofline lever per ROOFLINE.md). Design + implement the multi-CTA tiled GEMM pipeline (TMA + deep cp.async + swizzle), expose its dims to the autotuner (Stage 1 P1). Final tuning still needs the owner scale decision, but the infra build does not. Pick this up if the main queue empties.

content.subject: Switch SG11 gate: clamp(cos) -> sigmoid(gate_temp*cos)
content.description: Owner: switch SG11 cosine gating to sigmoid. CONFIRMED state: gate = clamp(cos_sim(grad,momentum),0,1) — a bare CLAMP that IGNORES the already-plumbed gate_temperature=5.0; code notes 'claims a sigmoid(t*cos) but does a bare clamp' (opt_stages_precompute.cuh:480). ## H3 (move-set hill-climb, task #13) — COMPLETE

Ran the dW + barrier lane as a loop, evidence-first. **1 move kept, then K=3 consecutive non-improving candidates → stopped.**

### Fresh baselines (HEAD c67cb66, profile-mode, single H100)

**d=1024 B=16384** — wall 1192.90 ms, 8.31 TF/s, 0.84% MFU
| phase | ms | % |
|---|---|---|

Confirmed the handoff: P2_dW_GEMM is the measured-biggest in-scope item @ d=1024.

### Move 1 — M-atom-interleave the dW tile path — **KEPT** (`a12c376`)

Root cause (verified in source): `dectc_dw_run_tile` / `dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk` called the GEMM engine with `MaxAtomsM=1, m_atoms=1` → `kIL=min(1,2)=1` → no interleave, exactly H1's noted gap. The engine + ring smem already support interleaved dW (the selftest's `gemm_dw_kernel` runs `MaxAtomsM=8, kIL=2`; `test_dw_random_multistep(Nout=512→8 atoms)` gates it) — only the **production driver** fed it 1 atom at a time.

Fix (decoder header only): a dW work item now owns a **group of up to `kDecDwIL=2` consecutive m64 atoms** → engine runs 2 wgmmas/k-step into independent fragments sharing ONE staged X-operand tile (overlap MMAs + 2× less X-operand HBM traffic on the K=T contraction). All decoder weights have even atom counts → split-K partial-scratch total unchanged; `DecTcSmem.sA` already had the room. Ascending-k preserved per atom → bit-exact.

**Gates (all green):** A/A/A ×3 bit-identical (sha `de94111a…`) + **parity bit-identical vs c67cb66** (rebuilt baseline+live, compared); `test_decoder_tc.py` 18/18 (incl. dW determinism + Nout=512 8-atom dW + full-cell oracle parity); `wiring_check --require-all` **33/33**; tail-gate adamw/decoder (Δp 2.4e-7, m 2.2e-7/v 9.6e-7) + muon/decoder (Δp 1.4e-6, state 0/0) PASS after production `_ops` rebuild.

Added a repeatable `-D KEY=VAL` knob to `tuning/decoder_bench.py` (loop infra). Clean throughput-only sweep:

G=1 wins @ d=1024 (saturated grid → split-K barrier+reduce is pure overhead) but loses +57% @ d=128 (few small dW tiles → idle SMs; split-K exists to fix this). G=8 ties @ d=128 (−0.27%, noise) but loses +2.4% @ d=1024. **No G beats G=4 at BOTH beyond noise → keep G=4** (the knob was already cross-scale-optimal). No code change, no rebuild needed.

### Move 3 — B1/barrier — **non-improving (deferred), evidence-based**

B1 wait (243.8 ms, 17.3% @ d=1024) is the fastest CTA spinning for the slowest: pure P1 **tile-count imbalance** (n_tiles=512 not dividing nCTA=132 → 4:3). Empirically probed the only gate-safe lever (kTileM): **kTileM=256 → B1 242.8 → 386.7 ms (+59%)**, becomes the dominant phase (worse 2:1 tail-wave); kTileM=64 would break H1's fwd/dX interleave (kAtomsM→1). The barrier is load-imbalance-bound; the real fix is dynamic work distribution = the cp.async-ring/task-queue restructure (**out of scope**).

### Move 4 — P1_bwd @ d=128 — **non-improving (deferred), evidence-based**

content.subject: Stage 3: roofline hill-climb at d=2048 (owner-authorized)

All three deliverables implemented, RUN for real on the single H100, and committed (`ef433ac` on top of `7656ea6`). Production `_ops` untouched — `wiring_check --require-all` = **33/33 L3-TC**. Tree clean except the 4 new files.

### DELIVERABLE 1 — `tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py` (+ `tests/hw/sharded_optimizer_binding.cu`), §7.3
At DP=1, `sharded_optimizer_kernel<Opt>` over the full param set is **BIT-IDENTICAL** to the in-kernel P3 fused tail. Used the task's equivalent check: production fused step (`return_grad=True`) → re-apply via the JIT-bound sharded kernel on the captured grad + zero state + the same `_opt_scalars_from` scalars. JIT-bound via `cpp_extension.load` into `/workspace/.torch_ext/sharded_opt_bind` (own build dir; production build never touched). Elementwise ids {adamw, lion, grokfast} × {decoder, vit, mamba}:
```
9 passed — every cell params bit-eq=True maxd=0.000e+00 | m_eq=True v_eq=True | grad_unmutated=True
```
**No loosening needed** — the assert is `torch.equal`, not a tol. Reason it's exact (not ULP): the kernel includes `opt_components.cuh` verbatim and calls the same `apply_optimizer<Opt>`; `rebase_state` only offsets per-element pointers, so flat-shard index `i` pairs the identical `(params[i], grad[i], m[i], v[i], ema[i])` + identical scalars as the per-tensor P3. The grokfast step-1 `ema[idx]=grad[idx]` cold-start replicates too.

### DELIVERABLE 2 — `tests/hw/test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py`, §7.1 + §6.4
`torchrun --nproc_per_node=2`, both ranks on `cuda:0`. NCCL 2.20.5 rejects two ranks on one device by default ("Duplicate GPU detected … ncclInvalidUsage") — defeated with a distinct `NCCL_HOSTID` per rank (the documented loopback workaround; verified `all_gather`/`reduce_scatter` then work). Per rank: production fused step on its batch shard → **fixed-order** grad reduce (`all_gather` + ascending-rank fp32 sum — the §2.7/§6.4 A/A/A non-negotiable, not raw NCCL reduce-scatter) → sharded-opt (DELIVERABLE-1 kernel) on the owned shard → `all_gather` params.
```
4 passed:
adamw/decoder:   (a) cross-rank bit-eq=True | (b) A/A/A bit-eq=True | (c) maxd=2.689e-05 rel=6.614e-06 (tol 3e-05) parity=True
lion/decoder:    (a) True | (b) True | (c) maxd=0.000e+00 rel=0.000e+00 parity=True
grokfast/decoder:(a) True | (b) True | (c) maxd=4.447e-05 rel=1.094e-05 parity=True
adamw/vit:       (a) True | (b) True | (c) maxd=4.414e-05 rel=1.178e-05 parity=True
```
(a) and (b) are **bit-exact**; (c) is within parity tol as the design predicts (DDP-equivalence: averaging two half-batch grads = the full-batch mean grad up to bf16 reduction grouping). The actual deltas are reported in-test.

**One non-obvious fix, documented in-file:** the eager DP=2 loopback initially *hung* — a rank busy-spinning in an NCCL collective starves the peer's full-GPU persistent megakernel on the shared device. Fixed by keeping per-rank device work **symmetric** (both ranks compute the (c) reference) + an explicit `torch.cuda.synchronize()` between every megakernel and every collective + `NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1`. Workers then tear down cleanly (no kill).

### DELIVERABLE 3 — `tests/hw/test_step_graph_capture.py`, §7.4
Captured `[ops.fused_step → sharded_optimizer_kernel]` as **one CUDA graph** on rank 0's stream, replayed 5×:
```
3 passed — every replay (adamw/lion/grokfast, decoder): bit-eq-to-eager=True maxd=0.000e+00 (N=5)
```
**Honest what-was/wasn't-captured (documented in-file):** the persistent megakernel captures fine (it's one launch). I verified per-piece that `fused-step`, `sharded-opt`, the combined no-collective chain, AND a standalone NCCL `all_gather` in the loopback all capture+replay. What is NOT robustly capturable on this 1-GPU loopback is **mixing the full-GPU megakernel with NCCL collectives across two ranks on one device** — a CUDA graph can't host the inter-op `synchronize()`s the eager loopback needed to dodge the megakernel-vs-collective SM contention. That mixed cross-rank capture is the genuine 8-GPU-window activity (one rank per device removes the contention), per §7.5. Shipped the §7.4-endorsed `[fused-step → sharded-opt]` fallback.

### Final gates
- New tests, consolidated: `16 passed` on 1×H100.
- Pre-work `test_parallel_instantiation.py`: `3 passed` (headers still compile).
- `wiring_check --require-all`: `33/33 L3-TC (100%)`, RC=0 — decoder 11/11, vit 11/11, mamba 11/11, all `path=L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)`.
- Tree clean: only the 4 new files committed; **zero tracked-file modifications**; the JIT binding builds outside the repo.

Relevant paths (all absolute): `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/tests/hw/test_sharded_optimizer.py`, `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/tests/hw/sharded_optimizer_binding.cu`, `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/tests/hw/test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py`, `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/tests/hw/test_step_graph_capture.py`.</result>

input.description: #19d: SG2/neuralgrok per-cell test isolation
input.prompt:
Task #19d in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, single H100, HEAD≈ef433ac (33/33 green). Fix the known TEST-STATE-LEAKAGE so the full 33-cell tail-gate suite can run back-to-back in one pytest invocation without false failures.

THE BUG (documented in the audit + reproduced before): running the full suite back-to-back, supergrok2/vit FALSELY fails ("kernel sharpness ~0 — SAM 2nd backward did not run", tests/hw/_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:~154) though it passes in isolation. Cause (per _sg2_l3tc_gate.py ~:198-203 and test_l3tc_tail_gate.py ~:179, ~:1042-1049): the per-op oracle (ops.supergrok2_batched_step) and the neuralgrok per-op path perturb a device-global (__constant__/global scratch) that the SUBSEQUENT TC launch reads -> sharpness collapses / NaN. Within-cell ordering+empty_cache mitigations exist (:204-218, :232-234); the missing piece is CROSS-CELL isolation.

FIX (test-side, per the audit's recommendation): subprocess-per-contaminating-cell isolation. Concretely: make the pytest entry for the SG2 cells (and neuralgrok cells if they cross-contaminate — verify) run their gate in a FRESH subprocess (python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell X already exists as a CLI — reuse it via subprocess.run, asserting on returncode + captured verdict line), so the device-global never crosses cells. Keep the in-process path for the clean cells (speed). Alternative if you find a cheaper guaranteed reset (e.g. an existing ops re-init/zero API for that scratch): prefer it; measure that it actually fixes back-to-back. DO NOT weaken any assertion; DO NOT touch kernel code.

VERIFY (the proof, on GPU): (1) reproduce the false-fail first on the CURRENT tree (run the suite back-to-back the way that triggers it — e.g. pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -m hw -k "supergrok2 or neuralgrok or adamw" in one process, or the documented repro) and capture the failure; (2) apply the fix; (3) the SAME invocation now passes; (4) the FULL suite `pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -m hw -q` passes 33/33 in ONE invocation (this is the headline — it has never been green back-to-back); (5) wiring_check --require-all still 33/33. COMMIT when green ("tests/hw: subprocess-isolate the per-op-oracle-contaminating cells — full 33-cell tail-gate green in one invocation (#19d)").

Raw outputs (the before-fail, the after-pass, the full-suite 33/33 line) + commit hash in the final message. If the repro does NOT trigger on the current tree (the leakage may have shifted with tonight's kernel changes), say so plainly, still add the isolation as defense-in-depth IF cheap, and report what you observed. No report files.

content.subject: Stage 3: roofline hill-climb at d=2048 (owner-authorized)
content.description: Owner authorized + clarified: an OPTIMIZATION LOOP UNTIL CONVERGENCE, not one-shot. Per cell: propose optimization (multi-CTA tiling / tile size / split-K / pipe-depth / smem / occupancy / autotuner winner) -> incremental rebuild (sccache) -> measure roofline % via tuning/roofline.py (min-of-N, quiet GPU) -> KEEP if % improves beyond the measurement-noise floor AND parity stays green, else REVERT -> repeat until K consecutive attempts yield no improvement = that cell converged (its ceiling). Then next cell. Final cross-cell sweep: components are shared, so a component-level win can lift multiple cells -> re-measure all. Run at d=2048 (adjustable 1024/4096 - flag before heavy GPU). Prereqs: all 33 cells built out + multi-CTA tiling infra (#14).

Branch claude/h100-audit-maximal. HEAD = 642e360. Tree CLEAN. wiring 33/33. Full tail-gate suite green in ONE invocation (first time ever). Production _ops rebuilt + verified 16:07Z.

## HEADLINE PERFORMANCE (the hill-climb, all parity/A-A-A-gated)
| metric | bedtime | now | factor |
|---|---|---|---|
| decoder d=1024 B=16k | 2084 ms / 4.75 TF/s / 0.48% MFU | **967.3 ms / 10.2 TF/s / 1.03% MFU** | **2.15x** |
| decoder d=128 (production) | 107.6 ms | **32.8 ms** | **3.28x** |
| vit d=128 (production) | 166.6 ms | **123.6 ms** (reg spills 6452B -> **0**) | 1.35x |
| mamba d=128 (production) | 108.0 ms | **102.7 ms** (255-reg budget held) | 1.05x |
| all-33 roofline | (eager base mean 0.38%) | **mean 1.15% / median 1.29%, all wgmma** | ~3x |

## THE 4 KEPT OPTIMIZATIONS (each: faster + parity green + A/A/A bit-identical + 33/33)
1. **H1** (627d134): M-atom-interleaved wgmma pipeline — 2 atoms share one staged B-tile, independent fragments -> MMA overlap + HALVED weight HBM traffic. d=1024 -22%.
2. **H2** (c67cb66): O(d·T) embed-grad CSR + single-owner bias reduce — grad_asm 520.7->8.7 ms (60x). Production 3.0x.
3. **H3** (a12c376): dW-tile interleave (the dW driver fed the engine 1 atom; now groups of 2). dW -30.7%.
4. **Ports** (5273f99, f560b89): H1+H3 -> vit (+ eliminated ALL its register spills) and mamba (within its zero-margin 255-reg budget; odd-atom x_proj handled).
Hill-climb stopped at K=3 non-improving (split-K G=4 proven cross-scale-optimal; barrier fix needs the big rewrite; P1_bwd at floor). 19 commits total tonight.

## VERIFICATION (the "test ALL functionality" mandate)
- #19 audit items ALL closed: (a) multistep parity gates implemented + GPU-PASS (grokadamw clip-fires-by-50 parity; prodigy d-adaptation tracks eager to ~1e-9, frozen-control diverges) (b) single-source warn->FAIL (+ found & fixed a stale symbol-table entry + comment-blindness) (c) hw-gate CI job added (d) subprocess isolation -> full 33-cell suite green back-to-back.
- Race smoke on the post-wins kernels: prodigy/decoder GROKS; SG11/decoder shows the documented memorize(0.958@150)->collapse; no DEGRADED, no nan, L3-TC path confirmed.
- Batch knees locked: decoder@d1024 B~=4096 (TF/s flat to 16k, slight DECLINE past); vit B~=16k; mamba <=4096.
- Phase-2 pre-tests (ef433ac): sharded-opt BIT-IDENTICAL 9/9 cells; DP=2 loopback cross-rank A/A/A bit-exact (fixed-order reduce); CUDA-graph step capture bit-exact x5. Only NVSHMEM-TP + real scaling measurements still need the 8x.

## HONEST FAILURES / OPEN ITEMS
- **cp.async mbarrier ring (the endgame rewrite): ATTEMPTED, cleanly REVERTED.** 3 structural blockers documented: (a) fp32 weights converted on read — cp.async/TMA can't convert, so the dominant operand can't stream async (fix = bf16 weight pre-stage phase or TMA descriptors); (b) dW operands transposed-strided -> TMA-with-transpose needed; (c) the shared engine is at 255 regs WITH 2.6KB spills — zero headroom for ring state. NEXT SESSION: attack (c) reg pressure first, then the ring. (The mbarrier/cp.async primitives already exist in-tree, silicon-validated, just unwired.)
- **#12 tuner GPU validation: INCOMPLETE.** Offline infra is committed+verified (84db23f), but the live run found the tuner's JIT path structurally broken — bindings.cpp pins PYBIND11_MODULE(_ops) so a JIT variant module can never import. The dead agent's diagnosis + partial patch preserved at /workspace/.orphan_12_jit_fix.diff. Tree reverted clean.
- **SG2 at ladder dims:** honest de-pin (7656ea6) exposed that SG2's workspace DESIGN doesn't scale (199GB @d1024). Bench now scopes it out (642e360, SASS-byte-identical for production). SG2-at-scale needs a workspace redesign (documented, not tonight).
- test_mamba_tc 3-fail: proven PRE-EXISTING (fails identically at the old HEAD); production mamba cells A/A/A green.

## 8xH100 DECISION (yours)
Phase-1 signal status: ladder buildable all 3 models (SG2 exception documented) ✓; parallelism authored + 1-GPU-validated ✓; megakernels maxed *within gate-safe scope* — one big known lever remains (the ring, needs the multi-hour structural work above).
- **Option A (my rec): one more focused 1x session** (~0.5-1 day): tuner-JIT fix + reg-pressure reduction + the ring (with the bf16 pre-stage), THEN provision 8x. The 8x window stays short and the per-GPU unit it scales is materially better.
- **Option B: provision 8x NOW** — distributed bring-up starts immediately; the ring work continues on one of the 8 in parallel. Faster calendar, more $/hr.
Either way the Phase-2 contract + pre-tests mean the 8x window is bring-up + measure, not design.

GPU idle since ~16:45Z, tree clean, all banked. Disk 17G root free (builds ate some; cleanup cycles ran all night). If you want to pause the 1x now and decide later: everything is committed; nothing in flight.
